claims.claim: France has no wealth tax on a portfolio: IFI covers real estate only

sources.name: Service-Public: impôt sur la fortune immobilière (IFI)
sources.says: Vérifié le 6 mars 2026. The IFI concerns a net taxable non-professional real-estate estate "supérieure à 1 300 000 €" on 1 January 2026; once over, tax starts from €800,000: 0.50% from €800,001 to €1.3M, 0.70% to €2.57M, 1% to €5M, 1.25% to €10M, 1.50% above. It is computed on the net value after debts relating to the taxable property. The page covers real estate only and names no financial assets.

sources.name: PwC: France, other taxes
sources.says: Last reviewed 24 April 2026. Real estate wealth tax applies only if net taxable real-estate wealth exceeds EUR 1.3 million on 1 January, at progressive rates from 0.50% (after an EUR 800,000 allowance) to 1.5% above EUR 10 million; "Only non-professional real estate properties are taxable." Inheritance: if the deceased is a French tax resident, worldwide assets are taxed; progressive rates apply after an EUR 100,000 rebate for direct-line beneficiaries.

sources.name: Ateis Patrimoine: Impôt sur la fortune improductive, ce que la LF 2026 a retenu
sources.says: Dated 1 April 2026, rewritten 13 May 2026. The impôt sur la fortune improductive was voted at first reading on 31 October 2025 but left out of the final 2026 finance law adopted on 2 February 2026; "aucun foyer fiscal n'est assujetti à un « IFIP » en 2026", so euro funds, cash and crypto stay outside the IFI base. "Aucun paramètre n'a été modifié par la loi de finances pour 2026": threshold €1.3M, scale 0.5% to 1.5%, and a 30% allowance on the main residence.

claims.note: Agrees with the France note in src/data/localTaxes.ts ("No wealth tax on a portfolio: IFI covers real estate only"); the model has no wealth entry for France. Gascony adds that IFI is "unlikely at rural Gers prices": no figure, not checked separately.

claims.claim: Dividends, interest and gains pay a 31.4% flat tax (PFU) from 2026: 12.8% plus 18.6% social levies

sources.name: PwC: France, income determination
sources.says: Last reviewed 24 April 2026. Dividends and interest earned from 2026 are taxed at a total of 31.4%: 12.8% income tax and 18.6% social surtaxes; capital gains are generally subject to the same 31.4% flat rate. The taxpayer may elect the progressive scale for all such income.

sources.name: Service-Public: social levies (CSG, CRDS) on income from assets and investments
sources.says: Verified 30 June 2026. On 2026 investment income in the general case: CSG 10.6%, CRDS 0.5%, solidarity levy 7.5%, total 18.6%. Life insurance, PEL, CEL and popular savings plans stay at 17.2% (CSG 9.2%), as does all 2025 investment income. Only people covered by the compulsory social security of another EU/EEA country or Switzerland are exempt from CSG and CRDS (7.5% solidarity levy still due); no non-EU country is mentioned.

sources.name: Expat.com: France raises flat tax to 31.4%
sources.says: Dated 10 March 2026. The flat tax rises "to 31.4%, up from the previous 30%" through a 1.4-point rise in the CSG from 1 January 2026 (9.2% to 10.6%, so social contributions go from 17.2% to 18.6%, plus 12.8% income tax). Life insurance, real-estate gains and unfurnished rental income keep the earlier rate.

also: sources: added Service-Public F2329 to all three

claims.claim: A 6.5% PUMa levy (cotisation subsidiaire maladie) can hit capital income above €24,030 for a resident with no pension or earnings

sources.name: Indy: simulateur de taxe PUMa (cotisation subsidiaire maladie) 2026
sources.says: Dated 14 September 2026. The contribution is due when earned income is below 20% of the PASS (€9,612) and capital income is above 50% of the PASS (€24,030; PASS 2026 = €48,060). Formula: 6.5% × (A − 0.5 × PASS) × [1 − R / (0.2 × PASS)], capital income capped at 8 PASS (€384,480). "Vous n'êtes pas redevable si vous avez perçu au cours de l'année : une pension de retraite", a disability pension, an annuity or unemployment benefit.

claims.note: Down the source order: www.urssaf.fr reset the connection on three tries (https://www.urssaf.fr/accueil/particulier/beneficiaire-puma.html twice, https://www.urssaf.fr/portail/home/espaces-dedies/beneficiaire-de-la-puma/assujettissement.html once), so the 2026 figures rest on a dated secondary page; the fact ends "check current rules". "No earnings" is loose: the levy tapers to nil at earned income of €9,612 (20% of the PASS). The levy is collected on the previous year's income. Nice's drawback "a possible 6.5% PUMa levy" agrees.

claims.claim: Under the treaty a US citizen (not French) who clearly intends to keep a US domicile and has lived in France under 5 of the last 7 years is treated as US-domiciled

sources.name: SF Tax Counsel: a closer look at the US–France estate and gift tax treaty
sources.says: Dated 16 November 2023. A citizen of one state is treated as domiciled there if "he had a clear intention to retain his domicile in that country" and "he was domiciled in the other country for less than five years during the 7-year period". "The situs country is given priority taxation in the case of real property, tangible personal property, and business assets"; double taxation is relieved by "requiring one of the countries to allow a credit against its tax for the taxes paid to the other country". It cites the 2004 Protocol.

sources.name: The Local France: the French 5-year rule for inheritance tax
sources.says: Dated 21 September 2023. For a French tax resident "France will consider your global assets for inheritance tax upon your death"; the treaty exception needs the person to have lived in France "less than five years during the 7-year period ending with the year of his death" and to be only temporarily there, in which case "only your French assets would be subject to French inheritance taxes".

claims.note: Both pages are from 2023, older than the plan's "dated 2025–26" for secondary sources; the treaty has not been amended since the 2004 protocol. The official consolidated text is a PDF on impots.gouv.fr (https://impots.gouv.fr/10conventionsetats-unisetats-unisconvention-avec-les-etats-unis-successions-donationsfd1836pdf) that WebFetch returned as unreadable binary, and no HTML copy was found; a person can check article 4(3) there. "(not French)" was not on either page read: the secondary page speaks of a citizen of one state domiciled in the other. Agrees with the localTaxes.ts note.

Resources of at least €1,477.93 net per month for one person over a year (€17,735.19 a year in the document list), from own income (annuities, pensions, rental income), bank certificates or sureties; family allowances don't count. Health insurance for the whole stay; a handwritten undertaking not to work in France. The card is valid "1 year maximum" and renewable, with the renewal filed online 4 to 2 months before expiry. Cost: €350 for a first application (€300 tax + €50 stamp duty), €250 for a renewal.

claims.note: Not in the profiles: validating the VLS-TS itself now costs €300.

claims.claim: Visitor-visa holders can join the public PUMa system after 3 months' residence

sources.name: Service-Public: protection universelle maladie (PUMa)
sources.says: Vérifié le 13 mai 2026. For a person who does not work, rights open only after 3 months' residence in France and continue if they live in France at least 6 months a year; non-EEA nationals need a residence document. The law of 30 December 2025 provides a financial participation for PUMa beneficiaries who live in France stably and regularly, have no professional activity and are not liable for CSG, CRDS or the health contribution under an international convention; a decree, which must set the amount, is awaited.

claims.note: ameli.fr (https://www.ameli.fr/assure/droits-demarches/principes/protection-universelle-maladie) returned HTTP 403; Service-Public is official too. The page speaks of anyone living in France stably and regularly with a residence document, not of the visitor visa by name. scores.healthcare unchanged.

claims.claim: The 2026 social security law added a health contribution for residents with no French work income who pay no French social levies under a treaty; its amount and scope await a decree (none as of Oct 2026)

sources.name: Service-Public: protection universelle maladie (PUMa)
sources.says: Vérifié le 13 mai 2026. For a person who does not work, rights open only after 3 months' residence in France and continue if they live in France at least 6 months a year; non-EEA nationals need a residence document. The law of 30 December 2025 provides a financial participation for PUMa beneficiaries who live in France stably and regularly, have no professional activity and are not liable for CSG, CRDS or the health contribution under an international convention; a decree, which must set the amount, is awaited.

sources.name: Easy France Now: the health contribution (CSS art. L160-1-1)
sources.says: Last checked 28 October 2026. Article L160-1-1, added by article 53 of loi n° 2025-1403 of 30 December 2025, covers people who live in France stably and regularly, have no professional activity in France and are not liable for the contributions of articles L131-9 and L136-1 under an international convention. The amount is "not set, because the decree it needs has not appeared"; no decree citing the article had been published as of 28 October 2026.

claims.note: The official page (13 May 2026) says the decree is awaited; the "none as of Oct 2026" date is from the secondary page's check of 28 October 2026. Whether one appeared between then and 2026-11-15 was not checked. Gascony's profile does not carry this clause.
